Forgiving  willing  to  pardon  or  excuse others' mistakes or wrongs. Generous -willing to give more  of something, especially money  or help, than is usual or expected.

items.text:
Sol.106.(a)  Negligent  failing  to  take proper care. Meticulous  showing  great  attention to detail; very careful and precise. Thorough  complete  with  attention  to every detail. Precise exact and accurate in detail. Careful  taking pains to avoid mistakes or harm.
Sol.107.(c)  Innovate  to  introduce  new methods or ideas. Imitate  to copy the actions, speech, or behaviour of someone. Replicate  to  make  an  exact  copy  of something. Copy  to  reproduce  the  same  as  the original. Echo to repeat a sound or statement.
Sol.108.(c)  Diminish -  to  become  or  to make something smaller or less important. Enhance -  to  improve  something  or  to make something look better. Increase -to become or to make something larger in number or amount.
Antonyms
Enlarge - to become bigger. Augment
- to increase the amount, value, size, etc. of something. Sol.109.(c) Vague -not clearly expressed or understood. Lucid expressed clearly. Transparent -allowing light to pass through or easy to perceive or detect. Clear  easy  to  perceive,  understand,  or interpret. Coherent -logically connected and consistent;  easy  to  understand  because
of clarity and organization.

Sol.110.(d) Malevolent -having or showing a wish to do evil to others. Benevolent -kind, generous, and well-meaning. Humane -showing compassion or kindness. Generous willing to give or share. Kind -having a friendly, gentle, or considerate nature.
Sol.111.(b) Reduce to make something smaller or less in size, amount, or degree. Inflate to fill something with air or gas; to increase in size or price. Increase to become or make greater in size, amount, or degree. Expand -to become larger in size, number, or importance; to spread out. Swell  to  become  larger  or  rounder  in size, often gradually or temporarily.
Sol.112.(b) Healthy -being in  good physical or mental condition. Wan pale, weak, or appearing ill. Tiring  causing  one  to  feel  in  need  of rest or sleep; exhausting. Long  having  great  length  in  space  or time. Wearisome  causing  fatigue,  boredom, or annoyance.

items.text:
Sol.113.(a)  Friendly showing kindness, goodwill, or  a  helpful  attitude  toward others. Hostile -unfriendly, antagonistic, or opposed to someone or something. Aggressive  ready  or  likely  to  attack, confront, or assert oneself forcefully. Rude  impolite  or  showing  a  lack  of respect toward others. Bitter  feeling  or  showing  deep  anger, resentment, or disappointment.
Sol.114.(b) Submit -yield to the authority,  control,  or  power  of  someone else. Dominate  have  control,  influence,  or power over someone or something. Rule exercise authority or control over a country, area, or people. Govern -to officially control or administer . Control the power to influence or direct behavior or events.
Sol.115.(b) Immature -not fully developed or grown. Mature - fully grown or fully developed. Developed - advanced or grown fully. Experienced -  having  knowledge  or  skill from practice. Grown - fully developed.
Sol.116.(b) Thoughtless -without consideration of the possible consequences. Prudent -showing good judgment, caution, and wisdom. Judicious having, showing, or done with good judgment. Cautious -careful to avoid  potential problems or dangers. Sensible  chosen  in  accordance  with wisdom or prudence.

items.text:
Sol.117.(a) Commend -to praise formally or officially. Vilify  to say or write unpleasant things about somebody/something. Malign to speak harmful untruths about someone. Slur an unfair or insulting remark. Defame to damage the good reputation of someone.
Sol.118.(a)  Forbid  to  order  someone not to do something. Authorize  to  officially  give  permission for something. Allow to let someone do something. Empower to give power or authority to someone. Permit to officially allow something.
Sol.119.(c) Fragile -easily  broken  or damaged. Resilient  able  to  quickly  recover  after something difficult. Tough physically or emotionally strong. Buoyant able to stay cheerful or recover quickly from difficulties. Flexible -able  to  bend  easily  without breaking.
Sol.120.(a)  Refuse -  to  say  firmly  that you will not do or accept something. Affirm -  to  state  clearly  or  publicly  that something is true. Accept -  to  agree  to  receive  or  approve something. Acknowledge -  to admit or recognize the existence or truth of something. Support -to agree with and give encouragement or help to somebody/something.
